tests.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: LCL / The Hush environment art study, test A of three.
Primary request: one richly observed, realistic cinematic environment concept painting of a future European municipal railway station still maintained for machines while human passengers are excluded. Landscape composition, approximately 16:9. This will be the architectural reference for two subsequent edited studies.
Scene/backdrop: a monumental but plausible concrete-and-steel railway hall in cool overcast daytime. An oblique eye-level wide view from the passenger concourse looks along two rails into daylight. Repeated concrete piers, an industrial clerestory, an overhead freight handling rail, elevated service galleries, and a precise autonomous freight trolley establish load and circulation. Keep a distinctive square pier in the middle distance, a closed waist-high passenger access gate near it, and a clearly visible small wall-mounted food dispenser and maintenance terminal nearby as anchors. A neglected wooden passenger bench and shallow water stains remain on the human concourse.
Subject and story: the freight rail, trolley contact surfaces, machine sensor windows, and operating corridor are immaculate and precisely serviced; abandoned passenger furnishings and inaccessible amenities are neglected. One ordinary adult in a simple worn work coat with a modest hand-tool bag waits outside the closed gate; the machine does not acknowledge them. No character identity or named location is established.
Lighting: readable diffuse daylight, small cold-white task lights over working machinery, sparse cyan status indicators. The food outlet is visibly clean and closed to the person, not glowing like a magical shrine.
Materials/textures: concrete with plausible drainage stains, clean brushed machinery, precise replacement covers, restrained local corrosion, old civic paint and useful service markings. Large calm surfaces establish scale. No universal layer of rust.
Style: grounded European public-infrastructure realism, tactile materials, exceptionally convincing construction and restrained colour. Art-directed photorealistic concept painting; not a game screenshot or film franchise imitation.
Composition/framing: stable architectural perspective, restrained wide lens around 35mm, camera at human height; clear foreground concourse, gate and terminal middle ground, operational freight corridor beyond. A generous clear area around the gate must allow later human additions without replacing architecture.
Constraints: same scene to be retained in later edits; include maintained and neglected conditions in one frame; original structure and serving function should read immediately; no title, labels, captions, watermark, giant billboards, heroic armour, fantasy machinery, giant holograms, supernatural aura, magenta colour wash, night rain, excessive cables, debris everywhere, permanent fog, or extreme bloom. Small incidental civic markings may be minimal, no need for prominent readable text.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: LCL / The Hush environment art study, test B of three.
Input image: edit target, station A. Preserve this exact station, camera position, perspective, image dimensions, concrete piers, clerestory, galleries, overhead freight crane and suspended container, rails, gate location, food dispenser, adjacent terminal, background buildings, diffuse daytime weather, and realistic materials.
Primary request: show the same passenger concourse carefully inhabited and maintained by a small Patchwork Republic community. Add human care to the existing architecture; keep the autonomous freight corridor precise and separate. The existing closed passenger gate still limits access, so the contrast with machine operation survives.
Changes: give the existing worn passenger bench a few beautifully fitted replacement timber slats and a folded personally embroidered cushion, retaining its recognizable form and position. At the left stair landing and beside the bench, add a compact well-organized communal worktable with fitted repair parts, numbered clamps, neat spools, hand tools within reach, and a small shared domestic corner with a kettle, decorated cups, a modest potted plant, one personal photograph, and a hand-painted small panel. Fit these additions to the accessible concourse edges without blocking routes or introducing new buildings. Add two ordinary residents using these spaces: one performing a careful repair and one making tea. Keep the original adult with their hand-tool bag near the gate at the same scale.
Human maintenance: a carefully routed drain repair and clean fitted floor plates create a visibly dry working island around the occupied bench and worktable. Keep damp patches where they were outside that maintained area. Use small documented replacement covers, inspection marks, and precise repairs rather than piles of junk. Give local domestic lamps modest amber warmth without changing daylight or tinting the entire scene.
Style: keep the source image's grounded European municipal infrastructure realism, photographic concept-painting treatment, natural scale, and cool neutral materials. Show affection, expertise, and simple beauty.
Constraints: only add the described human adaptations, repairs, ornament, and residents; preserve every architectural anchor and the freight system. No generic scrap-city clutter, new shrine, sci-fi armour, giant signs, magical effects, neon wash, heavy fog, excessive bloom, all-over rust, title, caption, border, or watermark. The final should be immediately recognizable as the same view.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: LCL / The Hush environment art study, test C of three.
Input image: edit target, station B showing human occupation. Preserve this exact camera, perspective, dimensions, daylight, station geometry, rail hall, piers, galleries, crane body and suspended freight container, rails, gate housings, dispenser, terminal, repaired bench, embroidery, repair worktable, plant, domestic objects, warm lamps, and two residents at their existing activities. Preserve the exact visual identity and clothing of the adult who waits near the gate.
Primary request: show a restrained, physically readable moment of LCL recognition in the same inhabited station. The waiting adult moves a short distance toward the existing wall relay terminal and extends one hand close to its surface, in a quiet ordinary gesture of communication. Their other hand retains the small tool bag. No heroic stance.
Changes only around contact and machine response: the existing waist-high gate panels swing open, leaving a clear safe pedestrian passage while retaining the metal gate housings and concourse edges. Existing small no-entry indicators become simple passage-status symbols. The adjacent food dispenser opens its delivery hatch and a plain cup is present inside, making accommodation tangible. The existing crane sensor face angles subtly toward the person and terminal, suggesting attention; keep the crane body, container, and load path in the same position. Small existing status lamps on terminal, gate, and crane share a restrained coordinated pale cyan/amber pulse. Very faint interference appears on the terminal's own glass only.
Interpretation: an already active world has noticed a person. The visual evidence is an open route, a provision outlet responding, a sensor orienting, and existing indicators coordinating. The workshop and ordinary care remain present; no environment-wide transformation.
Style: match the input image's grounded photographic European industrial concept art, quiet daylight, readable materials, and modest warm domestic corner. Keep the effect understated and focus on changed access and attention.
Constraints: preserve architecture and all human adaptations; change the waiting adult's position and hand gesture only as necessary for terminal contact. The other two residents remain as in B. No new characters, added giant robot, magical aura, glowing veins, floating UI, projected hologram, energy beam, sparks, levitation, particle storm, colour wash, dramatic new sunlight, neon takeover, captions, title, border, or watermark. This should look like a material system granting a response, not a fantasy spell.
